caption:
Operating tempo, this week: multiple reaches and corridors across the area of interest sat on scheduled revisit. Passes ran on cadence, day and night, regardless of cloud cover. Most returned quiet.

A small fraction of passes produced a change flag — a shift in water extent, a new thermal signature, a break in an established pattern of life. Each flagged pass moved to review. Most were resolved as benign after cross-check against prior imagery. A handful triggered a closer look.

This is the baseline. Not a single incident, not a single site — a standing collection plan running on schedule across a wide area, with the overwhelming majority of output being confirmation that nothing changed.
thread: Operating tempo this cycle: scheduled revisit across multiple reaches and corridors in the area of interest. Day and night, through cloud. Most passes came back quiet.
A small percentage produced a change flag. Each one went to review against prior-pass imagery before anything moved further.
Most flags resolved as benign. A handful warranted closer follow-up. That ratio is the point — the system is built to run quiet most of the time and surface the rest.
No incident, no site, no client in this post. Just the shape of the workload: continuous tasking, low noise, review before action.

card.headline: Most passes come back quiet
card.sub: Scheduled revisit across the area of interest, day and night, through cloud. Quiet is the baseline, not a gap.

rationale: Shows scale and discipline of ongoing monitoring without disclosing any specific site, client, or detection, reinforcing operational credibility through cadence rather than incident.
